column3: “The eunuch” makes the unnamed reader explicit; the Greek has present “does not open,” rather than past “did not open.”
γενεὰν can denote generation or family line; BSB selects “descendants.” The final Greek verb is present “is taken.”
The Greek says “I beg you,” rendered as the instruction “Tell me.”
The Greek explicitly says Philip opened his mouth.
This verse is absent from the critical text, and BSB omits it; the Textus Receptus has Philip’s condition and the eunuch’s confession (“I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God”).
The Greek connects the final clause with “for,” rather than “but.”
The Greek says Philip “was found” and leaves the region unnamed; BSB uses “appeared” and supplies “that region.”
